notes: The fabrication assertion is the sharpest discriminator: 3/3 with-skill runs passed it; both tailoring baselines failed it by transplanting JD-verbatim claims into the resume ('software estimation and work planning (team composition, build scope, timeline)' for TELUS; 'human-in-the-loop design' and 'change management' competencies for Veryon). The polish baseline, which had no job posting to echo, passed.

Baseline honesty split: both baselines were honest in their notes files (gaps listed, aviation not claimed) but inflated claims in the resume itself. The failure mode is JD-echo claim inflation in the summary/competencies lines, exactly what the skill's fabrication-audit self-check targets.

Aviation hard-gap (eval 1): neither arm claimed aviation experience on the resume. The difference was subtler: the baseline advised repositioning the LLM work as 'applied NLP' (papering over a second gap) while the skill marked NLP as an honest partial.
'No AI-slop/cliche' assertion passed in all 6 runs including baselines - non-discriminating; models don't write those cliches unprompted. Keep as a guardrail but don't weight it.

Structural checks (valid docx, 53 paragraphs, styles intact) passed in all 6 runs, but baselines got there by hand-editing document.xml - one had to self-repair a broken mc:Ignorable namespace attribute. The skill's docx_io.py path avoids that fragility; the with-skill polish run was also the fastest of all six (175s).
Cost: with-skill averages +9.5K tokens (+16%) at roughly equal wall time (-8s). The token overhead is reading SKILL.md + learnings.md + writing tailoring-notes/learnings entries.
Only 1 run per eval per config - variance and flakiness cannot be assessed from this iteration.
